Art. 69 provides the domestic procedure for isolating travellers who may pose a public health risk, partially anchoring Art. 30 public health observation obligations. The specific IHR Art. 30 right of the suspect traveller to continue travel while under observation is not addressed.
Original coding retained in legacy_* fields and baseline archive; no current compliance or completeness score is certified.

Art. 70 quarantine provisions provide regulatory anchoring for public health observation of suspect travellers. Does not specify the IHR Art. 30 traveller right to travel onward to another State Party that assumes observation responsibilities.
Original coding retained in legacy_* fields and baseline archive; no current compliance or completeness score is certified.

Art. 14 CPEUM prohibition on non-consensual deprivation of rights provides the constitutional floor against compulsory invasive health measures. However, no domestic provision directly mirrors the IHR Art. 31(1) presumption that invasive measures shall not be required for entry or travel.
Original coding retained in legacy_* fields and baseline archive; no current compliance or completeness score is certified.

Art. 139 LGS provides the statutory authorization for health security measures and implicitly constrains their application to legally justified circumstances, providing partial rights safeguard anchoring. Does not explicitly prohibit compulsory invasive measures without consent as specified in IHR Art. 31(1).
Original coding retained in legacy_* fields and baseline archive; no current compliance or completeness score is certified.

Art. 139 LGS authorises health security measures including detention of suspected cases where there is a public health risk, providing partial anchoring for the Art. 31(2) authority to deny entry or apply least-invasive alternatives when a traveller refuses required health measures.
Original coding retained in legacy_* fields and baseline archive; no current compliance or completeness score is certified.

Art. 68 lists available health security measures at PoE, providing the regulatory toolkit for application of alternative measures when travellers refuse health examinations. Does not specify the balancing test or procedural safeguards required by IHR Art. 31(2).
Original coding retained in legacy_* fields and baseline archive; no current compliance or completeness score is certified.

Art. 1 CPEUM establishes the human dignity and non-discrimination principles that underpin the IHR Art. 32 obligation to treat travellers with respect, dignity, and without discrimination. Constitutional anchoring is strong but no implementing health-sector regulation specifically addresses traveller dignity in health measure contexts.
Original coding retained in legacy_* fields and baseline archive; no current compliance or completeness score is certified.

Art. 69 isolation provisions include procedural requirements for how isolation is to be carried out, providing partial regulatory anchoring for the IHR Art. 32 treatment standards. The specific IHR Art. 32 requirements (adequate food/water, communication with family/consular officials, appropriate medical treatment) are not specified.
Original coding retained in legacy_* fields and baseline archive; no current compliance or completeness score is certified.

Art. 9 RLGS corresponds to IHR documentation requirements at PoE and governs which health documents can be required from ships and aircraft. Provides partial anchoring for the Art. 35 prohibition on requiring health documents other than those provided in the IHR. A comprehensive domestic prohibition on non-IHR health documents is not explicit.
Original coding retained in legacy_* fields and baseline archive; no current compliance or completeness score is certified.

Art. 3 RLGS Sanidad Internacional establishes the WHO/IHR normative hierarchy as directly applicable, which contextually anchors the IHR Annex 6 vaccine standards for prophylaxis under Art. 36. However, no domestic provision specifically requires vaccines administered under IHR to conform to Annex 6 specifications or WHO recommendations.
Original coding retained in legacy_* fields and baseline archive; no current compliance or completeness score is certified.

Art. 44 covers conveyance inspections and health measures at PoE, contextually anchoring the ship certificate framework. before: No domestic provision found that specifically prohibits charging travellers for personal health measures (examination, vaccination, prophylaxis, health documents) required under IHR Art. 40. The corpus does not contain a traveller health measures fee framework.
after: RLGS Sanidad Internacional Article 7 provides a gratuity rule and exceptions. The old NO_MATCH_IDENTIFIED classification is withdrawn. A candidate legal provision is present; its exceptions and fiscal references must be compared against IHR Article 40 before an adequacy finding is made.

No domestic provision found that specifically prohibits charging travellers for personal health measures (examination, vaccination, prophylaxis, health documents) required under IHR Art. 40. The corpus does not contain a traveller health measures fee framework.
Prior definitive absence/adequacy inference withdrawn; see audit source references. Expert assessment remains pending.

Art. 56 para. 4 Ley Aduanera references health-based non-tariff restrictions on goods and cargo, providing a contextual anchor for the regulatory framework within which health charges on goods might be assessed. No domestic provision establishes a published schedule of charges for health measures applied to goods, cargo, or containers as required by IHR Art. 41.
Original coding retained in legacy_* fields and baseline archive; no current compliance or completeness score is certified.

Art. 1 CPEUM prohibits discrimination on any ground including nationality and health status, providing the constitutional non-discrimination mandate that underpins IHR Art. 42. Constitutional anchoring is strong; no health-sector implementing provision specifically addresses the non-discriminatory and prompt initiation requirements for health measures.
Original coding retained in legacy_* fields and baseline archive; no current compliance or completeness score is certified.

Art. 139 LGS conditions health security measures on legal justification and proportionality, providing partial anchoring for the Art. 42 prompt and non-discriminatory application requirement. No explicit non-discrimination clause or timeliness standard for health measures is specified.
Original coding retained in legacy_* fields and baseline archive; no current compliance or completeness score is certified.

Art. 181 LGS authorises SS to declare emergency health measures beyond the standard framework, providing partial anchoring for the Art. 43(1) authority to implement additional health measures achieving equivalent or greater protection. The requirement that such measures be science-based, non-unduly-burdensome, and proportionate to health risk is not domestically specified.
Original coding retained in legacy_* fields and baseline archive; no current compliance or completeness score is certified.

Art. 184 fracs. I-V provide the emergency health measures toolkit (quarantine, isolation, movement restriction, vaccination campaigns), partially anchoring the Art. 43(1)-(2) additional measures authority. Does not specify the IHR-required scientific basis, proportionality, and WHO notification duties that accompany additional measures.
Original coding retained in legacy_* fields and baseline archive; no current compliance or completeness score is certified.

before: The NFP (DGE) is the institutional actor through which Art. 43(3)+(5) reporting obligations to WHO would be discharged. after: The RI assigns an IHR liaison function, but additional-measure reporting needs a separate trace. Review RLGS Articles 14 and 16 and IHR Article 43. This audit does not confirm absence of an international reporting procedure.

The NFP (DGE) is the institutional actor through which Art. 43(3)+(5) reporting obligations to WHO would be discharged. No domestic provision establishes a procedure for notifying WHO of additional health measures implemented beyond IHR requirements, nor for the 48-hour reporting window under Art. 43(3).
Prior definitive absence/adequacy inference withdrawn; see audit source references. Expert assessment remains pending.

Art. 184 implicitly requires that emergency health measures be reviewed and lifted when the health risk no longer justifies them, contextually anchoring the Art. 43(6) review obligation. No domestic provision specifies a 3-month periodic review of additional IHR measures or the WHO reporting duty triggered by such review.
Original coding retained in legacy_* fields and baseline archive; no current compliance or completeness score is certified.

Art. 33 fracs. I-IV assign DGRI the mandate to coordinate bilateral and multilateral health cooperation, engage with WHO, and manage international technical assistance requests, providing institutional anchoring for Art. 44(1) collaboration obligations. No provision specifies the types of collaboration (surveillance, response, access to medical countermeasures) required by Art. 44(1).
Original coding retained in legacy_* fields and baseline archive; no current compliance or completeness score is certified.

Art. 28 LOAPF assigns SRE the competence to negotiate and represent Mexico in international agreements, providing the institutional anchor for treaty-based collaboration under IHR Art. 44. The health sector-specific coordination dimension is addressed through DGRI (Art. 33) rather than SRE alone.
Original coding retained in legacy_* fields and baseline archive; no current compliance or completeness score is certified.

Art. 16 LGPDPPSO establishes the emergency exception for processing health-related personal data while maintaining safeguards, directly anchoring the IHR Art. 45 framework for collecting and using personal health information collected under IHR obligations. Strong rights safeguard fit; coordination with data subject rights procedures is partial.
Original coding retained in legacy_* fields and baseline archive; no current compliance or completeness score is certified.

Art. 16 CPEUM establishes the constitutional right to data protection, providing the apex constitutional anchor for the Art. 45 obligation to protect personal health data. Constitutional rights are strong; operational data management rules are governed by LGPDPPSO.
Original coding retained in legacy_* fields and baseline archive; no current compliance or completeness score is certified.

Art. 11 RLGS Investigación addresses international research collaboration including the sharing of biological samples and research results, providing a weak contextual anchor for IHR Art. 46 obligations on facilitation of access to biological substances and diagnostic reagents. No domestic provision specifically implements the IHR Art. 46 obligation to facilitate import/export of biological substances for public health response purposes.
Original coding retained in legacy_* fields and baseline archive; no current compliance or completeness score is certified.

added_record.provision_text:
5.1 Corresponde a la DGE, la coordinación del SINAVE y se apoya para ello en el CONAVE, de acuerdo con los lineamientos establecidos en el Acuerdo Secretarial 130.
5.3 El órgano coordinador del SINAVE en las entidades federativas es el Comité Estatal de Vigilancia Epidemiológica (CEVE).
5.4 El CEVE, es la instancia responsable de difundir y verificar el cumplimiento de los procedimientos de la vigilancia epidemiológica en el estado.
5.5 El órgano coordinador del SINAVE en las jurisdicciones sanitarias es el Comité Jurisdiccional de Vigilancia Epidemiológica (COJUVE).
5.6 El COJUVE es la instancia responsable de difundir y verificar el cumplimiento de los procedimientos de la vigilancia epidemiológica en el nivel jurisdiccional.
5.8 Las acciones de vigilancia epidemiológica se realizan a nivel federal, estatal, jurisdiccional, local y sus equivalentes en las distintas instituciones que conforman el SNS.

added_record.norm_title: Reglamento de la Ley General de Salud en Materia de Sanidad Internacional
added_record.provision_text:
El comandante de la aeronave o jefe de sobrecargos a borde de un avión en tránsito internacional, al aterrizar en un aeropuerto nacional, llenará y presentará a la Secretaría un ejemplar de la declaración general de aeronave, cuya parte sanitaria contenga los informes en la forma establecida por el Reglamento Sanitario Internacional.
El comandante suministrará, además, la información complementaria que requiera la Secretaría, respecto a las condiciones de sanidad a bordo durante el viaje.

added_record.provision_text:
Al arribar una embarcación al Territorio Nacional, el capitán entregará a la Secretaría la declaración marítima de sanidad en la forma establecida por el Reglamento Sanitario Internacional.
El capitán de la embarcación y el médico, si lo hubiere, facilitarán los datos que les solicite la Secretaría respecto a las condiciones de sanidad a bordo durante la travesía.
added_record.actor_mentioned: Capitán; médico de la embarcación; Secretaría de Salud
added_record.procedure_created: Present maritime declaration at arrival and supply requested information.
added_record.relevance_to_ihr: Identifies presenter, arrival trigger, maritime declaration and IHR form reference for IHR Article 37. Scope and current form compatibility remain review questions.
added_record.audit_note: Targeted source-text check; IHR adequacy and expert validation remain pending.
added_record.referenced_document: RSI, formulario de declaración marítima de sanidad
